questions: What exactly counts as a "standard delimiter" — spaces only, or also commas, tabs, newlines?
Should consecutive delimiters be treated as a single separator, or produce empty strings between them?
Are leading or trailing delimiters expected to produce empty-string entries in the output array?
Is punctuation attached to a word (e.g., "word,") considered part of the delimiter or part of the word?
What should be returned for an empty input string?
Should the split be case-sensitive in any way relevant to word boundaries?
Are numeric tokens or symbols treated as "words" the same as alphabetic tokens?
Is the order of words in the output array expected to match their order of appearance in the input string?
answers: Consecutive delimiters are treated as a single separator, as the test with 'One,, two' yields no empty strings.
No, leading or trailing delimiters do not produce empty strings, as shown by the test with trailing comma.
For an empty input string, return an empty list, as shown by the test case.
Case-sensitivity is not relevant; words are split based on delimiters, and case is preserved as in the input.
Yes, the order of words in the output matches their appearance in the input, as shown by the examples.
